meta_description: Enterprise Risk & Scenario Intelligence — composed architecture, platform stack and the metric the program answers to.

blocks.x: A no-theater description of Enterprise Risk & Scenario Intelligence: what ships first, what it touches at operational stores, how it is verified, and the per workflow metric we commit to moving against baseline.
The problem this solution exists for
Risk models live in separate estates with manual scenario assembly; stress tests consume quarters; early-warning arrives with the loss.
Our approach

We build the risk analytics spine: governed models with explainability, scenario engines run jointly by finance and risk, early-warning sensors wired to decision hubs, and documentation produced as you build.
Reference architecture

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Enterprise Risk & Scenario Intelligence
blocks.note: The pipeline is measured end to end; each stage reports its own freshness and cost, which is what makes the unit economics arguable.

blocks.x: We engineer Enterprise Risk & Scenario Intelligence so that regressions are cohorts, not surprises: each stage owns its latency budget and failure policy, and rollback is rehearsed before go-live rather than after the incident.

items: Stress and what-if scenarios with finance-risk workflow
Scores flowing to limits, pricing and actions

blocks.x: Platform stack

The solution runs on EEMS Platform and Driisti Smart Vision Glasses: Enterprise decisions in milliseconds — with a full evidence trail for each decision. Model governance your risk committee and regulator can review.

items: We measure the starting position and lock the baseline with your team — no build work begins before the number is agreed.

Runbooks, enablement and the control trail that let your teams operate it without us in the room.
Quarterly re-audits and a ranked backlog of the next decisions worth automating — value that accumulates on purpose.

blocks.x: Prerequisites and data readiness

The readiness work for Enterprise Risk & Scenario Intelligence is unglamorous and decisive — data contracts, access paths and owner names. Programs that skip it discover the gaps at the first gate, which is the most expensive place to find them.
How a delivery runs

A delivery for Enterprise Risk & Scenario Intelligence runs on rhythm, not ritual: the baseline is signed in the first weeks, evidence is generated as the work happens, and the gate at each stage has real stop authority. Programs that miss their evidence stop.
